subject: Winthrop Street Gardener Cap and Rules Revision
overview: The Community Garden Commission voted to cap the number of gardeners at Winthrop Street for the upcoming season and reviewed garden rule models from other cities. The commission also discussed potential locations for new 'pocket gardens' and off-season planning.

items.title: Garden Updates
items.summary: Members discussed compost progress at Winthrop Street and the recent installation of a new storage shed at Berry Park.

items.title: Compost Tumbler Disposal
items.summary: Mark Lalli offered a rodent-proof compost tumbler for use at another site, leading to a discussion about placing it at the Tufts or Berry Park gardens.

items.title: Pop-up Garden and Future Locations
items.summary: The commission discussed removing the pop-up garden fence and potential future use of the beds at the West Medford Community Center.

items.title: Pocket Gardens and Site Planning
items.summary: The body discussed forming a subcommittee to meet with city officials to identify small 'pocket garden' sites that would not require Parks Commission approval.

items.title: Winthrop Street Capacity Cap
items.summary: Approved a motion to cap the Winthrop Street garden at 62 gardeners for the 2027-2028 season. The garden steering committee will determine the method for distributing the remaining full-sized plots.

items.title: Rules and Infractions Discussion
items.summary: Liz White presented a summary of community garden rule structures and infraction policies from Somerville and other municipalities to guide future local revisions.

items.title: Future Garden Planning
items.summary: Discussion focused on utilizing small city parcels and contacting the MBTA regarding green space near Wellington Circle for potential community use.

items.title: Meeting Schedule and Off-Season Activities
items.summary: The commission agreed to return to a Tuesday meeting schedule and discussed collaborating with other local organizations for winter educational programs.
